extraction_metadata.extraction_notes: Single flowchart table, section '2 Flowchart', printed rotated 90 degrees on four portrait letter pages (document pages 8-11); the header band (study period / visit / week / window) reprints on every page and is de-duplicated to schedule_property rows 1-4. Grid read mechanically: rule lines recovered from a 200 dpi render (vertical image rules = table row boundaries, horizontal image rules = table column boundaries because of the rotation), text-layer tokens from pdftotext -bbox assigned to the resulting cells. 1 leading label column, so the first data column is position 2 and the 25 data columns run 2-26. All 378 marks are literal 'X'. An independent near-black-pixel raster detector reproduced the mark matrix for all 69 body rows with zero disagreement. Inline protocol section/appendix references printed in activity labels are emitted as deduplicated source_note annotations with synthesized markers pr1-pr29.

table_metadata.table_purpose: Primary schedule of activities for the whole trial: screening, run-in, randomisation, maintenance period, end of treatment and end of trial visits.
table_metadata.notes: Only one table in the excerpt. table_type main_soa: rows are procedures performed on subjects, it is the primary anchor grid, and there is no second column structure or second population to compare against. Although the grid runs over four pages, the source presents it as one continuous, unnumbered flowchart with a reprinted header band rather than as separately titled tables, so it is modelled as a single table with page_start 8 / page_end 11 rather than one main_soa plus three continuation tables. The epoch header row is the only row carrying merged cells (Run-in 3:12, Maintenance period 14:24); every body row has a complete set of internal column rules, so no body mark is merged.

schedule_properties.property_comment: Top header band naming the study periods that group the visit columns: Screening, Run-in, Randomisation, Maintenance period, End of treatment, End of trial. The row-label cell is empty in the source, so the property_name is synthesized. Classified as 'epoch' because the values are major study phases.
Visit identifiers, one per column: V1, V2, P3 ... V25. The label distinguishes site visits (V) from phone contacts (P). Classified as 'visit' because the values are named/numbered visit identifiers.
Nominal timing of each visit expressed in study weeks (-1, 0, 2 ... 75). Classified as 'week' because the values are week numbers relative to randomisation week 20 / run-in start week 0.
Permitted visit window in days for each column ('-7 to 0', '0', '±3' ... '0 to +5'). Classified as 'window' because the values are visit tolerance windows, not timepoints.
